info.title: School Timetable Maker API
info.description: Backend API for the School Timetable Maker application. Provides endpoints for managing schools, admin authentication, academic years, grades, streams, sections, subjects, teachers, teacher eligibility, subject requirements, section subject teacher assignments, the schedule configuration, the timetable feasibility report, timetable generation and generated timetable versions.

post.summary: Register the first admin of a school (setup token required)
post.description: Creates the FIRST admin of a school. It needs the one-time setup token that was returned, once, when the school was created (POST /api/schools), or that an operator issued with the recovery command. The token is single-use, bound to this school and expires (24 hours by default). It is consumed only if the admin is actually created: a validation error does not use it up. Every reason a token is refused (unknown school, wrong token, expired, already used) gives the same 401, so the response says nothing about which schools exist. A school that already has an admin refuses a second registration (409): further admins are added by an authenticated admin with POST /api/admins. Rate-limited to 3 per hour per client.

post.summary: Create grades with streams and sections (bulk, atomic)
post.description: Create up to 20 grades for one academic year, each with its streams (up to 10) and sections (up to 30; 200 sections per request), in ONE all-or-nothing transaction: either the whole structure is created or nothing is. The academic year must belong to your school and be DRAFT. Every field follows the single-record endpoints (POST /api/grades, /streams, /sections). Rules: grade name and displayOrder unique (in the request and in the year); stream code (case-insensitive) and name unique per grade; section code unique per (grade, stream); a grade is streamed or not, never mixed: if any section has a "streamCode" every section of that grade must, and it must name a stream declared in that grade; streams may be declared without sections. Request rule violations are 400 and conflicts with existing grades are 409, both with "errors" keyed by row ("grades.0.sections.2.streamCode"). The response nests streams and sections under each grade, with ids.

post.description: Create 1-100 teachers in the authenticated admin's school in ONE all-or-nothing operation. Each row follows POST /api/teachers (name 1-200 chars; optional employeeCode trimmed/uppercased/max 50, empty = none; optional isActive, default true). A repeated employeeCode inside the request is 400; one that already exists in the school is 409; both are keyed by row ("teachers.2.employeeCode") and nothing is written. The Idempotency-Key header (8-128 chars of letters, numbers . _ : -) is REQUIRED and is stored with the teachers in the same transaction: retrying the SAME key with the SAME body returns 200 with the original result ("replayed": true) and creates nothing; the SAME key with a DIFFERENT body is 409. Simultaneous requests with one key create the teachers once. A failed request stores nothing, so its key may be reused. Keys are scoped to the school. Teacher subjects and grade eligibility are separate calls, unchanged.

No academic-year status rule applies. "type" is PRIMARY or SECONDARY (the teacher's primary or secondary subject); it has no effect on eligibility, assignment or generation; it only orders substitute candidates (a link of either type marks a teacher of the subject, PRIMARY first). This link is the teacher's SUBJECT QUALIFICATION and is always required before the teacher can be assigned. "gradeScope" (optional) says which grades the teacher may teach this subject in: SELECTED_GRADES (the default when omitted: only grades with an explicit POST /api/teacher-subjects/{id}/grades row, entered per academic year) or ALL_GRADES (every grade, an explicit choice; no grade rows are needed). post.description: Define the school's standard weekly schedule for an academic year: the working days, the number of teaching periods per day and exactly ONE break per day, given as the period it comes after (breakAfterPeriod, 1..periodsPerDay-1). There are no clock times, break durations or other timing events: timetables are generated from period numbers and the break position only. The break is not a teaching period, so it never counts toward subject requirements or teacher workload; weekly teaching capacity = working days x periodsPerDay. One configuration per academic year, shared by every grade. The academic year must be DRAFT. The old `periods` and `timingEvents` fields are refused (400). Half-days, exams and holidays are NOT part of this configuration. periodsPerDay and breakAfterPeriod are strict integers (strings and booleans are rejected).

post.summary: Start generating a timetable for a DRAFT academic year (asynchronous)
post.description: Queues a generation run and returns 202 immediately; nothing is solved inside the request. A quick preflight rejects requests that cannot work (unknown or foreign year, year not DRAFT, Module 10 readiness NOT_READY). The background runner then repeats every check on a fresh snapshot, so the preflight is a courtesy and not the authority. Poll GET /api/timetable-generations/{id} until status is SUCCEEDED or FAILED. A successful run creates a NEW DRAFT timetable version; nothing is overwritten or published. The time limit, worker count and solver process are server-side policy and cannot be set here. Only one run per academic year can be QUEUED or RUNNING. With options.sourceVersionId the new draft keeps the locked lessons of that DRAFT exactly. The locks are frozen and preflighted at this request (400 LOCKS_INVALID with the detailed issues if they do not fit the current configuration; 404 SOURCE_VERSION_NOT_FOUND; 403 for another school's version; 400 SOURCE_VERSION_WRONG_YEAR; 409 SOURCE_VERSION_NOT_DRAFT) and validated again, authoritatively, by the run. If no timetable that keeps them can be produced the run FAILS (LOCKS_INVALID, INFEASIBLE_HARD_CONSTRAINTS when proven impossible, or NO_SOLUTION_WITH_LOCKS when none was found in time, which does not prove impossibility): nothing is persisted and the source is untouched. Without locks the baseline fallback always exists; with locks it is best-effort and may be absent, in which case the new version's baselineMetrics says {available: false}. An academic year holds at most MAX_DRAFTS_PER_YEAR (default 20) draft versions: an active generation reserves one slot, so the request is refused with 409 data.code DRAFT_LIMIT_REACHED (data.drafts, data.maxDraftsPerYear) when the year is already at the cap. Delete or publish a draft first. A run queued before the cap was reached can still FAIL with failure.code DRAFT_LIMIT_REACHED at the end (nothing is created).

post.summary: Publish a draft timetable; the previously published version is archived
post.description: One transaction: the draft becomes PUBLISHED and the version that was published until now becomes ARCHIVED, so an academic year never has two published versions and never loses its published version because a publish failed.
